problem: MLLMs handle 360° panoramas by splitting them into multiple perspective views, leaving ERP spherical geometry (latitude-dependent distortion, seam wrap-around, observer-centered directions) implicit. Prior panoramic MLLM work is fragmented across single tasks and lacks a capability-level formulation and a unified benchmark.
motivation: Full-surround sensing matters for navigation, robotic search and 3D scene understanding, yet perspective-based pipelines fragment observations and need iterative multi-step exploration. Generic MLLMs fail on ERP spatial questions such as BFOV grounding, reference-frame transformation and viewer-centered 3D reasoning. The authors argue that large-scale pano-native supervision plus geometry-aware adaptation is needed.
key_idea: Fine-tune Qwen3.5 on 3M capability-aligned instruction samples built from a verified panorama metadata graph (570K ERP images), and inject spherical geometry into ViT patch tokens via Spherical Spatial Cross-Attention (SSCA).
insight: The capability-data ablation shows panoramic understanding is compositional: spherical data drives localization, reference-frame data drives relational reasoning, depth data drives 3D reasoning, and all four together are best. Verification of the metadata gives a large gain (38.8→55.1 overall). Early patch-level cross-attention beats residual addition and later insertion (55.1 vs 51.5 best residual), and updating the vision encoder and interface matters, since LLM-only tuning is clearly worse on seam and relation categories. Prompting with a coordinate grid helps only coarse localization.
method: ERP corpus: 570,321 panoramas (52.2% indoor / 47.8% outdoor) from Realsee3D, 360+X, web crawling, street-view and API sources, with seam, blur and geo-duplicate filtering.
Geometry-aware detection metadata: render 120° FoV views at 60° yaw stride, run WeDetect-Large, reproject to ERP, and verify by confidence, NMS and cross-view ERP IoU>0.6.
Language-grounded semantic metadata: Qwen3-VL-32B generates category, attributes and a referring phrase; WeDetect-Ref-4B re-detects and the entity is kept only if IoU>0.7.

Depth-aware metadata graph: aligned depth or pseudo-depth from a panoramic depth model gives per-entity distance; nodes carry semantics, angular footprint and depth, and edges carry spherical and 3D relations. 7.65M candidate QAs are sampled down to 2.998M instructions across semantic, angular, reference-frame, depth and seam tasks.

SSCA: after patch embedding, sinusoidal-encoded yaw/pitch of patch centers pass through an MLP into spherical tokens S; visual tokens attend to S with multi-head cross-attention and are fused through a learnable small-init gated residual, leaving the pretrained backbone otherwise unchanged.
Training: full fine-tuning of Qwen3.5-9B on 8×A100 (AdamW, lr 1e-6, 1 epoch). For VLN, PanoWorld-VLN is fine-tuned on R2R/RxR (80% of the data) with only the ERP panorama as input.
PanoSpace-Bench: 2,000 questions (8 categories × 250) on images disjoint from training; multiple-choice accuracy plus BFOV angular mIoU with seam wrap-around.

results: PanoWorld raises Qwen3.5-9B on PanoSpace-Bench from 30.8 to 56.5 overall, versus the best baseline Mimo-v2.5 at 37.2. Zero-shot on H*Bench it reaches 56.1 versus 38.4 for the best perspective-view baseline (HVS-3B), and 70.1 after H* SFT. On R2R-CE val-unseen with panorama-only input it gets 54.3 SR / 52.1 SPL, beating StreamVLN (50.2 / 47.1) and GridMM (49 / 41).
limitations: Metadata comes from automatic detectors, MLLM annotation and pseudo-depth, so errors can propagate despite the two verification steps.
PanoSpace-Bench is static and diagnostic; it does not cover long-horizon interaction, dynamic scenes or multi-agent navigation.
VLN details (action space, history handling, decoding) are thin, and the comparison mixes data budgets and observation types.
